cannot_judge: Crossfall / cross-slope of the kerb lane

criteria.room: Kerb lane is driveable for a van along most of the 597 m, but it's already heavily used for resident parking in chunks 1, 2 and 4 — cars line the kerb almost continuously near the Frederick St/Woodstock Ave ends. The clearest open stretch is the park frontage in chunk 3 (roughly 500–560 m along), with few driveways to dodge.
criteria.frontage: Mostly two-storey houses close to the road for chunks 1, 2 and 4. Chunk 3 faces a grassed park/oval with scattered trees on the kerb side, giving a stretch with no houses directly opposite.
criteria.overlooked: Houses sit close to the kerb (5–10 m) with upstairs windows facing the street in chunks 1, 2 and 4 — several driveways and front yards open straight onto the line. The park-facing stretch in chunk 3 is not overlooked at all.
criteria.slope: Mean grade 5.4%, max 16.6% — this is a steep, continuously descending street (44 m to 18 m over 597 m). Chunk 3 is the steepest section (~7%). The only comfortable spot is the flattest 20 m (0.1% grade), which falls near the end of chunk 3 into chunk 4, close to the park and the Frederick St intersection.
criteria.disturbance: Residential through-street, not a dead end — chunk 4 ends at a busier cross-street with a car park/more traffic, which will add noise near that end. Elsewhere it reads as a quiet suburban street.
criteria.shade: Good tree cover throughout, especially over the park stretch in chunk 3 — decent morning shade, some risk of sap/leaf drop from overhanging canopy.
criteria.signs_vs_imagery: No painted islands, bike lanes, bus zones or build-outs visible in the imagery; markings are consistent with the parallel-parking signs in the data. Esri (2025) and QLD (2022) agree closely — the main QLD-only detail is the still-vacant/bare lot in chunk 2, now landscaped in Esri.

reasons: Steep street overall, only one short flat stretch
Flat spot sits beside the park, unoverlooked
Rest of kerb lined with cars, close to houses
summary: Mostly too steep to sleep level; one flat, unoverlooked stretch by the park near Frederick St.
